newsitem.title: UK: Midland Ind bid could top two stg per share.
newsitem.headline: Midland Ind bid could top two stg per share.

text.p: Mirror Group Plc may have to pay more than two stg per share for Midland Independent Newspapers Plc, analysts said on Tuesday.
"I think we'd be looking at something in excess of two pounds," said Ben Thefaut of broker Albert E.Sharp.

David O'Brien of BZW, looking at multiples paid for other local newspaper groups, came up with a valuation of 192-222 pence per share. He said the likely price was somewhere in the middle of that range, around 207p.
Midland Independent said earlier on Tuesday that it was in talks with national newspaper group Mirror, which may lead to an offer being made for the company.
Midland shares surged 30p to 179p, having earlier touched a high of 190p. Mirror slipped 3.5p to 205p.
A price of at least two pounds per share would value Midland at upwards of 275 million stg.
Floated in 1994 at 140p, the company publishes seven paid-for titles and 29 freesheets in the city of Birmingham and other parts of the English Midlands.
Its flagship title is The Birmingham Post, while it also publishes the Evening Mail in the same city and the Evening Telegraph in nearby Coventry.
Mirror and Midland are partners in cable television channel Birmingham Live.
Mirror does not have any local newspaper operations but was rumoured to have tried to buy Pearson's Westminster Press business last year.
Westminster Press, publisher of more than 50 local titles, was bought by Newsquest Media Group for 305 million stg last August.
That deal was one of several in the sector over the past 18 months and analysts said a rival bidder for Midland Independent could emerge.
Big players in the sector include Newsquest, backed by U.S. buy-out specialists KKR, Trinity International Holdings, Northcliffe Newspapers, United Provincial UWS.L and Johnston Press.
